body.statement: For the constructed law \(P^{\star}\), the corrected PT vector is \(q_{\mathrm{PT}}(P^{\star})=(0,0)^{\prime}\), its profiled normal \(R_{\mathrm{PT}}\) has rank one, and \(P^{\star}\in\mathcal M_I\). The uniquely identified SC weights are \((1/2,1/2)\), while minimizing the PT Gram criterion over donor weights summing to one gives inverse-change-variance weights \((4/5,1/5)\). The union QP therefore fixes the final donor coefficients at \((1/2,1/2)\); its required SC preperiod-normal coefficient differs from the SC oracle coefficient, so both one-sided Gram discrepancies are strictly positive. Hence \(V_U>\max\{V_{\mathrm{PT}},V_{\mathrm{SC}}\}\). The same inequalities hold on a relatively open region preserving full rank, unequal positive donor-change variances, and unequal SC and PT-oracle weights.
body.justification: The witness proves that the adaptation frontier has empirical content and is not an algebraic relabelling of the PT-efficient score.
body.gap: ChenSantAnnaXie2025 shows covariance-optimal PT weighting, and SunXieZhang2025 identifies SC weights from preperiod means, but neither paper exhibits a legal intersection region where the two canonical gradients differ and union regularity is strictly costly.
body.consumer: The witness is a calibration design for simulations that test software implementing the union quadratic program and its standard errors.
